description: Conformance vectors for what one poll of the failsafe control plane heard (mythos_core.failsafe.wire: poll_outcome, PollOutcome and its heard_clean). Typed by hand as an answer key, never generated from the code it checks. A control plane that sets the two headers, and a product that reads a poll without this core, each hold themselves to the core with one test against this file. 'words' is the closed set of words for how a read ended, each with its reader's sentence. 'answers' are answers that arrived: 'status', 'body' (the body's text, exactly) and 'headers' (name to value; a name is matched whatever its letter case) are the input, with 'truncated' (whether the HTTP client could not call the body complete). 'no_answer' are reads that ended with no answer: the word offered is the input. Every 'expect' gives the outcome's fields: 'ended', 'status' (null when no answer arrived), 'commands' (how many commands were read), 'unreadable' (the plane's count; null when its header is there and is not a whole number, which is not a count of zero), 'skipped' (entries of a decoded body that were not read as a command), 'in_force' (the stops its header names, always in 'in_force_order', strongest first, whatever order was sent; empty when the header is absent and when it cannot be read), 'in_force_unreadable' (the header is there and cannot be read), 'truncated' and 'heard_clean'. The in-force header names every kind of stop in force on the page the plane answered, inside its command's window or not, as a comma-separated list of distinct words; spaces and tabs around each element are dropped; an unknown word, another letter case, an empty element, a word twice or two values make the whole value unreadable, and nothing of it is kept. heard_clean is true only for a 200 whose body was decoded and was whole, with an unreadable count of exactly 0, nothing skipped, and in_force_unreadable false. It is not 'the engine may run': a poll heard clean can carry commands and can name stops in force, and a stop named there may also be among the commands. The file holds only printable ASCII. Every engine, key and nonce here is invented. 'lines' are answers whose header lines are given as sent ('lines': each line's name and value, in order), with 'headers' the one value per name the HTTP client joins them into (the values in order, joined by a comma and a space). A header sent on more than one line is two values: 'expect' is the outcome when the client's own list of the lines is read (X-Failsafe-Unreadable is then null, X-Failsafe-In-Force unreadable, and the poll is not heard clean), and 'expect_joined' the outcome when only the joined value can be read.

words.heard: The control plane answered 200 and its answer was decoded.
words.unreachable: No answer arrived: the read was refused before it left, or it failed on the way.
words.timed_out: No answer arrived inside the read's time bound.
words.refused: The control plane answered with a status that is not 200.
words.undecodable: The control plane answered 200 and its answer could not be decoded.
words.unknown: Nothing is known of how the read ended: the channel cannot say, or the poll raised.
